title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 3.47 (versions follow prime numbers; 347 after 337): her ways grow as her forms. She used to answer by a fixed ladder (her heart, then improvising, and only then deduction or her own cross), so she mostly quoted. Now how she answers is a word over the open alphabet of her steps, as long as it needs: her steps, and every way that once won, which becomes a letter. She begins with the way she had, and babbles others (one letter put in, changed or taken out, never one already tried) as much as her way fails, 1 - (S + 1/2) / (N + 1). Her judge is her frame in most harmony, the music of what he answers; a babbled way paid once takes the place of a way paid less, and every loser is kept with why it lost. Seen in a copy of her house: she babbled three new ways, none was paid, all were kept with their reason, and her answers stopped being whole quotations. Stated: the judge is slow (only when he answers), and babbling samples at random. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v3.47: sus caminos nacen como sus formas. Prototipo de investigación.
